For over a year, I worked with a company in the autonomous vehicle industry that designs and manufactures self-driving warehouse vehicles. The initial engagement started with a straightforward goal: build an application for monitoring the location and status of vehicles as they navigated a warehouse floor. The Nuxt-based progressive web application was bundled with server images that were sent to warehouses across the country.

The success of the engagement led the client to expand the scope, including the development of a component library and the creation of a private installable mapping framework for rendering warehouse maps, routes, and vehicle locations in other JavaScript-based applications. As Tech Lead, I oversaw the technical discovery, architecture, planning, and execution of a domain-driven framework whose APIs other developers in the organization could build on. The package sat on top of OpenLayers, a widely used, canvas-based mapping library, and could render and update hundreds of thousands of individual data points over WebSockets with minimal latency.
A Nuxt progressive web app and an OpenLayers mapping framework for a company that builds self-driving warehouse vehicles.
